title_en: Preventing disasters with AI and robots... Government creates 10.5 billion won ‘National Safety Industry Fund’
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] The government plans to create a dedicated fund worth 10.5 billion won to foster disaster safety companies with cutting-edge technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and robots. The plan is to support the advancement of technology and products and business expansion of promising companies by attracting private funds using government investment as a priming agent. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety announced on the 31st that it will promote the formation of the 'National Safety Industry Fund No. 1', which is operated as a fund of funds, National Safety Account, to foster promising companies in the disaster safety field. This fund is an investment fund dedicated to the disaster and safety field that is raised with the Ministry of Public Administration and Security as a priming fund. This is a method of investing intensively in disaster safety companies with cutting-edge technologies such as AI and robots, in which the government invests funds and adds private investment. Korea Venture Investment, a fund management institution, conducted a public offering, document screening, on-site inspection, and presentation screening. Hyundai Motor Securities was finally selected as the fund manager after comprehensively evaluating the possibility of early fund formation and investment performance. Hyundai Motor Securities is currently managing 14 funds with a total of KRW 431.1 billion. Among them, it also has experience in managing two fund-of-funds in the environment and water industries with KRW 90 billion. title_en: Netflix stock price plunges 40%... Past slumps bounce back without fail
summary_en: [GD Net Korea] Netflix's stock price has fallen more than 40% from its all-time high last year, marking the seventh plunge since the IPO in 2002. Each time it fell more than 40% in the past, it rebounded significantly, but as growth has slowed compared to before, attention is being paid to whether past trends will repeat. According to The Motley Fool, an American financial investment media outlet, on the 31st (local time), Netflix stock prices have rebounded about 16% in the past five weeks, but are still more than 40% lower than the all-time high recorded in June of last year. Netflix's stock price has fallen more than 40% from its peak since the IPO in 2002. This is the seventh time. In the past, various negative factors, ranging from intensifying competition to failed business strategies and a decline in subscribers, brought down the stock price. In 2004, the stock price fell 64% as price competition with then-rival Blockbuster Online intensified. In 2011, the company's strategy to separate its streaming and DVD rental businesses led to consumer backlash, causing its stock price to fall by 82%. In 2022, the shock of subscriber decline was significant. As Netflix announced an unexpected decline in subscribers, concerns about its growth potential spread, and its stock price plunged 76% from its peak. After plummeting 71% immediately after the IPO, it remained at its lowest point for 12 months...
